title: Interactive railkit and token orchestration for cost lenses
creator: Ava Brooks
description:
Problem: The cost dashboard is using multiple ad-hoc component variants for compact lists, rollout rails and density-sensitive metric chips. This creates inconsistent spacing, mismatched token usage across breakpoints, and extra implementation QA for engineering.

Goal: Create an interactive "railkit" (a set of composable rails/rows and micro-rail components) and an orchestration layer of tokens that govern spacing, elevation, focus states and density adjustments for cost lenses (cost-summary, cost-breakdown, and active-rollouts). Produce a Figma variants catalog, CSS token mapping, and a small prototype that demonstrates responsive behavior, state transitions, and accessibility states.

Scope:
- Define token set: spacing (rail-padding, chip-gap), typography scales for compact/regular/expanded lenses, elevation tokens for micro-cards, focus/hover color tokens, and motion durations for rollout transitions.
- Design atomic rail components: left-icon rail, metric-rail, control-rail (for rollout toggles), and nested micro-rail for action chips.
- Build Figma library file with component variants and a usage page documenting how to compose rails into cost lenses.
- Prototype interactions: hover/focus outlines, keyboard navigation within rails, and adaptive density toggles.
- Provide engineering handoff artifacts: token-to-CSS mapping table, example markup snippets, and an acceptance QA checklist.

Success criteria:
- Single source token set consumed by at least two cost view pages (cost-explorer and rollout-inspector) in a staging build.
- Figma library has 90% coverage of the rail variants used in the console.
- Engineering report shows a 30% reduction in variant-specific CSS and a 25% faster QA cycle for visual regression tests.

Links and artifacts:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/console-railkit-v2
- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Railkit+Design+Spec
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4242
- Accessibility notes: https://docs.accessibility.redwood.ai/console/railkit-a11y

Acceptance criteria:
1) Design tokens documented and exported as a JSON token map.
2) Figma library contains named variants and usage examples for density 3-point scale.
3) Prototype demonstrates keyboard focus ring and ARIA attributes for rails.
4) Handoff includes CSS variable mapping and two example implementations (cost-explorer and rollout-inspector).
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: scoped deliverables with PM and Eng. Agreed to limit initial token set to spacing, elevation, color states, and motion. Diego to prepare initial token draft.

2026-02-25 - Early sketch review: PM prefers compact-first approach for PLG flows; highlighted need for explicit quota display slot in metric-rail. Action: add a compact chip variant with truncated tooltip behavior.

2026-03-01 - Figma iteration 1 uploaded. Notes: consolidated three chip variants into a single component with density property; added keyboard nav prototype. Request from Eng: include CSS variable names in Figma spec layers.

2026-03-03 - Accessibility review with Security & Accessibility team: color contrast of secondary chip falls short at compact sizes. Updated token recommendation for secondary-foreground to meet 4.5:1 at smallest text size.
2026-03-06 - Engineering sync: ENG suggests exposing two elevation tokens (rail-elevation-1, rail-elevation-2) rather than per-component elevation to simplify theming. Accepted and updated token map.

2026-03-08 - Design critique: UX lead requested clearer affordance for canary rollouts inside control-rail and proposed a subtle shimmer motion to indicate live traffic. Motion duration bounded to 120ms to keep CPU cost low.
2026-03-10 - Handoff prep: exported token JSON and added CSS variable mapping doc. Next: demo the prototype to Console PMs and schedule engineering intake for sprint planning.

Open follow-ups: finalize naming conventions for tokens (prefixed with --console-rail-), create Jest visual regression baseline for three density states, and pair with ENG on theme toggles for high-contrast mode.
